title: Rate limits are regenerating capacity defined by a maximum and a per-day slope, not fixed caps
content:
A.6.1.1.6.2.6.1.2.2.1.3.4 gives the formula: the contract "will calculate and return the minimum of (slope * time elapsed since lastUpdated + lastAmount) and maxAmount." Pattern's USDS mint limit is configured with `maxAmount` 100,000,000 USDS and `slope` 50,000,000 USDS per day (A.6.1.1.6.2.6.1.2.1.1.3.1.1.1), with the USDS-to-USDC swap limit set the same way.

This is a leaky-bucket allowance rather than a ceiling. Two independent quantities are bounded at once: the largest single action (capped by current available capacity, itself capped by `maxAmount`) and the sustained rate over time (capped by `slope`). A cap alone would permit an unlimited number of max-size actions in succession; a rate alone would permit an unboundedly large single action after a long idle period. Combining them closes both.

Capacity is also **restored by reversing the action**: burning USDS "will increase the available Rate Limit for minting USDS by the amount of USDS being burned," explicitly "limited by the `maxAmount` parameter" (A.6.1.1.6.2.6.1.2.2.1.2.1.2.1.2.1). Round-tripping therefore does not consume the day's allowance, so unwinding a position is never throttled by the size of the position that was opened.

The control has an off switch: `setUnlimitedRateLimitData` (A.6.1.1.6.2.6.1.2.2.1.3.3) sets `maxAmount` to `type(uint256).max`, and `getCurrentRateLimit` then short-circuits to unlimited. That switch is admin-only — which, per the role definition, means Sky Governance.
description: Available headroom accrues as min(slope x elapsed time + lastAmount, maxAmount), so a large action drains capacity that refills over days — bounding both single-transaction and sustained throughput.
